newsitem.title: CHINA: China banks to hold policy meeting in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: China banks to hold policy meeting in Beijing.

text.p: Senior officials of the People's Bank of China -- the central bank -- and other financial institutions will meet in Beijing next week for a national policy conference, officials said on Monday.

Around 1,000 officials of the People's Bank, commercial banks, insurance companies and other entities would gather to review progress in the financial sector over the last year and set policy for 1997, a central bank official said.

"The meeting will touch on all aspects (of work in the finance sector)," the official said but declined to give any details of the agenda for the annual conference, which this year will be held from January 13 to 17.
Financial structural adjustment was likely to be an important issue at the meeting, said an official of the People's Bank in southern Guangdong province.
The central bank would continue to try to prevent duplication of efforts in the financial sector, the official said by telephone.
Tight monetary controls and tough anti-inflation policies upheld at the 1996 meeting would be reaffirmed again this year, he said, but gave no details.

The need to curb illegal underground banks and money lenders that provide high-interest loans to borrowers who cannot access credit from state-run financial institutions has also been reported as high on the meeting's agenda.

Beijing has repeatedly called for a tightening of management of the financial sector, which has struggled to keep up with change in the booming economy, saying illegal banks and funds cause financial chaos and undermine state economic policies.
